article_title: Teaching resources for the European Open Platform for Prescribing Education (EurOP2E)—a nominal group technique study
citation: Bakkum, M. J. et al. (2022). Teaching resources for the European Open Platform for Prescribing Education (EurOP2E)—a nominal group technique study. npj Science of Learning. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41539-022-00141-y
title: EurOP²E — the European Open Platform for Prescribing Education
description: EurOP²E is a platform that "seeks to improve and harmonize European clinical pharmacology and therapeutics (CPT) education by facilitating international collaboration and sharing problem-based, online, open educational resources." It was set up to address the EACPT Education Working Group's recommendation 6, that schools utilize more online learning resources and share them nationally and internationally. Depending on the theme, its function will vary from supporting international communication and collaboration to providing teach-the-teacher materials and initiating collaborative production of ready-to-use teaching materials.
requirements: Open (free to re-use, adapt, and redistribute) distribution of resources
Teacher participation and collaboration across countries
constraints: Must be dynamic as educators' resource needs change with growing collaboration
Local/national differences in electronic prescribing systems must be accounted for when making such resources available for international use
target_learners: Medical and pharmacy students in European CPT education
target_learning_goals: Clinical pharmacology and therapeutics knowledge, skills and attitudes
examples: Participants proposed and ranked 35 teaching materials across four online meetings to inform what the platform should host
key_sources: Bakkum, M. J. et al. (2022). Teaching resources for the European Open Platform for Prescribing Education (EurOP2E)—a nominal group technique study. npj Science of Learning. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41539-022-00141-y

article_title: An Approach to Integration: The Integration of Language and Content to Promote L2 Learner Autonomy at the College Level (Un Acercamiento a la Integración: El Aprendizaje Integrado de Lengua y Contenidos para Promover la Autonomía del Estudiante de Lengua Extranjera en la Universidad)
citation: Oliva Parera, P. M., & Núñez Delgado, M. P. (2015). An Approach to Integration: The Integration of Language and Content to promote L2 Learner Autonomy at the College Level. Gist Education and Learning Research Journal, 10, 92-112. https://portal.issn.org/resource/ISSN/1692-5777
title: European Language Portfolio (PEL) adapted for the American graduate university context
description: The European Portfolio for Languages, developed by the Language Policy Division of the Council of Europe, contains three distinctive elements: the "language passport" identifying the learner's skills, the "language biography" described as the axis of the portfolio where students reflect upon and evaluate their progress, and the dossier for storing information or skills. This research adapted the portfolio for use in a graduate university context at an American university, aiming to broaden the research base of the PEL regarding portfolios' role in encouraging student autonomy.
requirements: Teachers must consider what students say when analyzing their own work, since metacognition relates to students' control of learning situations
Portfolio sections including assessment needs, linguistic bibliography, and long- and short-term learning goals
constraints: The original PEL was developed in conjunction with the CEFR for the European community; this study adapted it to the American graduate context
target_learners: postgraduate university students learning a foreign language
examples: Students submitted portfolios at the end of the semester; experimental-group extracts show goals tied to MBA, environmental studies, and career language needs
key_sources: Oliva Parera, P. M., & Núñez Delgado, M. P. (2015). An Approach to Integration: The Integration of Language and Content to promote L2 Learner Autonomy at the College Level. Gist Education and Learning Research Journal, 10, 92-112. https://portal.issn.org/resource/ISSN/1692-5777

article_title: The Feasibility and Quality of the European Prescribing Exam: An International Multicenter Pilot Study Among 3109 Medical Students From 16 Medical Schools.
citation: Donker, E. M., Piët, J. D., Brinkman, D. J., Richir, M. C., Papaioannidou, P., Likic, R., Sanz, E. J., Christiaens, T., Costa, J. N., De Ponti, F., Böttiger, Y., Kramers, C., van Agtmael, M. A., & Tichelaar, J. (2026). The Feasibility and Quality of the European Prescribing Exam: An International Multicenter Pilot Study Among 3109 Medical Students From 16 Medical Schools. Clinical Pharmacology and Therapeutics. https://doi.org/10.1002/cpt.70063
title: European Prescribing Exam
description: A free-of-charge, standardized, cross-border online examination on safe prescribing developed through the Erasmus+ project EuroPE+ by nine medical schools, the EACPT, and the NVKFB. Each exam comprises "a knowledge part, containing 24 unique (case-based) multiple-choice questions (MCQs) and 12 unique multiple-answer medication review questions (MAQs), and a skills part containing 11 unique questions" on prescribing for clinical case scenarios. It is implemented as a formative examination, conducted in English, and covers eight main drug topics.
requirements: An assessment blueprint covering the first three levels of Miller's pyramid
Peer review of all questions by senior clinical pharmacologists and other medical specialists
constraints: Administered in English due to over 20 European languages
Students may use guidelines and formularies for the skills part but not for the knowledge part
target_learners: Fifth- and sixth- (final-) year medical students
target_learning_goals: Safe and effective prescribing knowledge and skills
examples: Administered to 3109 students from 16 medical schools in 11 European countries between October 2020 and August 2023
key_sources: Donker, E. M., Piët, J. D., Brinkman, D. J., Richir, M. C., Papaioannidou, P., Likic, R., Sanz, E. J., Christiaens, T., Costa, J. article_title: Performance of single-agent and multi-agent language models in Spanish language medical competency exams.
citation: Altermatt Fernando R., Neyem Andres, Sumonte Nicolas, Mendoza Marcelo, Villagran Ignacio, Lacassie Hector J. (2025). Performance of single-agent and multi-agent language models in Spanish language medical competency exams. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-07250-3
title: Curated EUNACOM question dataset of 1,062 Spanish-language medical licensure items
description: The study curated a dataset of "1,062 publicly available and previously administered EUNACOM questions", preprocessed with orthographic standardization and exclusion of image-based or multimodal content. Answer choices were randomized per run to minimize ordering biases, and each item carried a predefined correct answer used as an automated evaluation key. The dataset served as the benchmark for comparing ten prompting and multi-agent strategies on GPT-4o.
requirements: Questions must be multiple-choice with predefined correct answers to support fully automated scoring
constraints: Image-based and multimodal content was excluded, so results do not cover multimodal exam items
target_learners: medical trainees and physicians preparing for the Chilean EUNACOM licensure exam
target_learning_goals: specialized medical knowledge assessment across 21 medical specialties in Spanish
examples: GPT-4o was evaluated on the dataset under ten strategies, each tested twice at three temperature settings
key_sources: Altermatt Fernando R., Neyem Andres, Sumonte Nicolas, Mendoza Marcelo, Villagran Ignacio, Lacassie Hector J. (2025). Performance of single-agent and multi-agent language models in Spanish language medical competency exams. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-07250-3

article_title: Using simulation to teach nursing students how to deal with a euthanasia request.
citation: Demedts, D., Magerman, J., Goossens, E., Tricas-Sauras, S., Bilsen, J., De Smet, S., & Fobelets, M. (2024). Using simulation to teach nursing students how to deal with a euthanasia request. PLoS One. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0299049
title: Euthanasia simulation module for nursing students: online learning module, good-practice video, role-play scenarios, and DML debriefing
description: A simulation module developed to prepare nursing students for dealing with a euthanasia request. In the authors' words, "three key components were incorporated: a preparatory phase consisting of an online PowerPoint, a good-practice video, and a simulation scenario; a simulation role-play; and a debriefing session." The module's content was validated by four Belgian end-of-life care experts, and it was completed by 17 final-year nursing students from two University Colleges in Flanders, Belgium.
requirements: Students complete a preparatory online learning module covering conversation techniques and the legal framework before the simulation session
Content validated by domain experts in end-of-life care
constraints: Focused on the first phase of the euthanasia process, initial care and accompaniment, not the later phases
Conclusions apply only to nursing students, not other healthcare students
examples: Three scenarios were enacted per session: one around cancer, one around polypathology, and one around unbearable mental suffering euthanasia
key_sources: Demedts, D., Magerman, J., Goossens, E., Tricas-Sauras, S., Bilsen, J., De Smet, S., & Fobelets, M. (2024). Using simulation to teach nursing students how to deal with a euthanasia request. PLoS One. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0299049

article_title: Developing translational medicine professionals: the Marie Skłodowska-Curie action model.
citation: Petrelli Alessandra, Prakken Berent J., Rosenblum Norman D., EUtrain fellows. (2016). Developing translational medicine professionals: the Marie Skłodowska-Curie action model. Journal of Translational Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12967-016-1088-1
title: EUtrain Marie Skłodowska-Curie ITN program for translational medicine training
description: EUtrain (EUropean Translational tRaining for Autoimmunity & Immune manipulation Network) was a Marie Skłodowska-Curie innovative training network funded in 2011 that provided 3-year doctoral research training to early-stage researchers with diverse backgrounds across academic institutes and companies. It aimed to provide "education on professional and personal skills, mentoring, and long-lasting network of TMPs." Fellows conducted joint research projects, received network-wide training events such as a grant writing weekend and workshops on presentation skills, communication, moderation of scientific meetings, valorisation of results and intellectual property.
requirements: Joint research projects within a worldwide network
Regular mentorship on career and personal development by experienced TMPs
target_learners: early-stage researchers (basic scientists, biotechnologists, medical doctors, chemists, engineers)
examples: Work Package 2 included 4 joint research projects held by 4 early-stage researchers located in academia and industry, focused on biomarker identification and validation
key_sources: Petrelli Alessandra, Prakken Berent J., Rosenblum Norman D., EUtrain fellows. (2016). Developing translational medicine professionals: the Marie Skłodowska-Curie action model. Journal of Translational Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12967-016-1088-1

article_title: Developing translational medicine professionals: the Marie Skłodowska-Curie action model.
citation: Petrelli Alessandra, Prakken Berent J., Rosenblum Norman D., EUtrain fellows. (2016). Developing translational medicine professionals: the Marie Skłodowska-Curie action model. Journal of Translational Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12967-016-1088-1
title: Eureka Institute week-long translational medicine course and community
description: The Eureka Institute, founded in 2007, is a worldwide community of over 200 fellows trained in interdisciplinary teamwork, open-minded thinking and principles of translational medicine during a week-long course held in Siracuse, Italy. Teaching comprises interactive sessions led by experts including scientific directors, journal editors, industry, and patient organization representatives. "To maximize the learning experience, the training technique requires students to work together to design strategies and solutions to real-life issues previously encountered by experienced TMPs." The network maintains meetings, seminars, social-network sharing, and a database under development.
requirements: Long-term sustainability to provide fellows access to continuously updated knowledge and tools
target_learning_goals: translational medicine principles including intellectual property, funding, regulation and trial design
examples: Fellows are trained in leadership, teamwork and communication to different types of audience as well as ethical and technical principles of the translational medicine machinery
key_sources: Petrelli Alessandra, Prakken Berent J., Rosenblum Norman D., EUtrain fellows. (2016). Developing translational medicine professionals: the Marie Skłodowska-Curie action model. Journal of Translational Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12967-016-1088-1

article_title: Essential competencies in prescribing: A first european cross-sectional study among 895 final-year medical students.
citation: Brinkman DJ, Tichelaar J, Schutte T, Benemei S, Böttiger Y, Chamontin B, Christiaens T, Likic R, Maˇiulaitis R, Marandi T, Monteiro EC, Papaioannidou P, Pers YM, Pontes C, Raskovic A, Regenthal R, Sanz EJ, Tamba BI, Wilson K, de Vries TP, Richir MC, van Agtmael MA. (2017). Essential competencies in prescribing: A first european cross‐sectional study among 895 final‐year medical students. Clinical Pharmacology & Therapeutics. https://doi.org/10.1002/cpt.521
title: A European CPT core curriculum with clear learning outcomes, early real‐life prescribing experience, and a robust assessment structure should be developed
description: The article recommends that undergraduate CPT education be restructured around a core curriculum with defined outcomes and practical prescribing experience. Specifically, it suggests "a European CPT curriculum should be developed with clear learning outcomes, emphasis on gaining early experience of drug prescribing for real patients in a clinical setting and completing prescriptions" alongside a robust European assessment structure ("European Prescribing License") to ensure outcomes are met. This responds directly to the study's finding of widespread inadequate prescribing competencies.
requirements: Clear learning outcomes for CPT education
Emphasis on early experience of drug prescribing for real patients in a clinical setting
A robust assessment structure to ensure outcomes are met
constraints: Curricular change is described as a slow and demanding process
target_learning_goals: knowledge of drug interactions and contraindications
examples: The study found 46.2% of therapies inappropriate and 54.7% of prescriptions containing errors, motivating the recommendation for curricular reform
key_sources: Brinkman DJ, Tichelaar J, Schutte T, Benemei S, Böttiger Y, Chamontin B, Christiaens T, Likic R, Maˇiulaitis R, Marandi T, Monteiro EC, Papaioannidou P, Pers YM, Pontes C, Raskovic A, Regenthal R, Sanz EJ, Tamba BI, Wilson K, de Vries TP, Richir MC, van Agtmael MA. (2017). Essential competencies in prescribing: A first european cross‐sectional study among 895 final‐year medical students. Clinical Pharmacology & Therapeutics. https://doi.org/10.1002/cpt.521

article_title: Integrating Numerical Computation into the Modeling Instruction Curriculum
citation: Caballero, M.D.; Burk, J.B.; Aiken, J.M.; Thoms, B.D.; Douglas, S.S.; Scanlon, E.M.; Schatz, M.F. (2012). Integrating Numerical Computation into the Modeling Instruction Curriculum. http://www.vpython.org/
title: Iterative Euler-Cromer motion-prediction algorithm as the shared computational core across force and motion models
description: The article teaches a four-step algorithm applied locally in space and time: compute the net force, update velocity with Newton's 2nd law, update position with the new velocity, and repeat. Formally this is "explicit (Euler-Cromer) numerical integration" of the equations of motion. Because the models differ only in net force and initial conditions, changing initial conditions or net force produces qualitatively different simulations, highlighting commonality among the no-forces, balanced-forces, and unbalanced-forces models.
requirements: Knowledge of the system's initial position and velocity and the net force on the system
A computer to handle the labor-intensive iterative calculations
target_learners: high school physics students in algebra-based or calculus-based courses
target_learning_goals: predicting motion using Newton's second law and kinematics
generalizing across force and motion models
examples: Students generalized a constant-acceleration program to the parabolic motion model simply by giving the object an initial velocity with nonzero horizontal and vertical components
key_sources: Caballero, M.D.; Burk, J.B.; Aiken, J.M.; Thoms, B.D.; Douglas, S.S.; Scanlon, E.M.; Schatz, M.F. (2012). Integrating Numerical Computation into the Modeling Instruction Curriculum. https://arxiv.org/abs/1207.0844

article_title: Transforming High School Physics with Modeling and Computation
citation: Aiken, J. M. (2013). Transforming High School Physics with Modeling and Computation. Georgia State University. https://scholarworks.gsu.edu
title: Euler-Cromer numerical integration algorithm for Newtonian motion prediction
description: The thesis introduces a four-step computational algorithm for predicting motion: at a given instant compute the net force, then compute the new velocity using Newton's 2nd law, compute the new position with the updated velocity, and repeat from the updated time. The thesis states that "the iterative application of Steps (1)-(3) is, in effect, explicit (Euler-Cromer) numerical integration of the equations of motion for Newtonian mechanics." Students were told to update velocity using net force divided by mass, emphasizing the force's relationship to the equations of motion.
requirements: Students are given initial position and velocity and the net force on the system; a short time step drives each update.
constraints: Applied to force and motion models described by Newton's 2nd law; the thesis confined its computational extensions to constant velocity, constant acceleration, balanced forces, and unbalanced forces models.
target_learning_goals: linking net force and Newton's 2nd law to program updates
examples: Students used Euler-Cromer integration in all computational activities to determine velocity and position after each time step.
key_sources: Aiken, J. M. (2013). Transforming High School Physics with Modeling and Computation. Georgia State University. https://arxiv.org/abs/1310.3725

article_title: The Future Quantum Workforce: Competences, Requirements and Forecasts
citation: Franziska Greinert, Rainer Müller, Philipp Bitzenbauer, Malte S. Ubben, Kim-Alessandro Weber. (2023). The Future Quantum Workforce: Competences, Requirements and Forecasts. arXiv:2208.08249. https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.08249
title: European Competence Framework for Quantum Technologies
description: A framework developed in the QTEdu CSA that "aims to map all possible competences, knowledge and skills, that could be relevant for the future quantum workforce and its development". Its structure emerged from this study's categorization: theoretical background, practical background, and QT applications. Version 1.0 (May 2021) has eight domains, including concepts of quantum physics, enabling technologies, hardware, quantum computing and simulation, sensors and metrology, communication, and practical and soft skills. It has been used for Qualification Profiles and to map and compare modules and courses.
requirements: Used as a common language to map and compare modules and courses; concrete measurable competences and proficiency levels were to be added in the follow-up QUCATS project
constraints: Version 1.0 competences are mainly content-specific and lack proficiency levels, which were only added in version 2.0 from April 2023
target_learners: future quantum workforce in industry and academia
target_learning_goals: quantum technology competences, knowledge and skills across theoretical, practical and application domains
examples: The beta version was compiled from the main 1 categorization and shared for community feedback; expert interviews in Spring 2021 led to version 1.0
key_sources: Franziska Greinert, Rainer Müller, Philipp Bitzenbauer, Malte S. Ubben, Kim-Alessandro Weber. (2023). The Future Quantum Workforce: Competences, Requirements and Forecasts. arXiv:2208.08249. https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.08249
